name: GeneralSettings
description: General settings tab within the runner Settings panel. Displays application-level preferences for startup behavior plus the runner's two optional feature disclosures. Contains 'Application' (Auto-load Last Configuration on Startup, Launch on System Startup) and 'Optional Feature Sets' (Show advanced automation features, Show visual GUI automation), and — only while the advanced disclosure is on — 'Workflow Builder' (Include AI Summary in New Workflows). All settings are boolean toggle switches. The startup and workflow toggles persist via Tauri IPC with optimistic updates and rollback on failure; the two disclosure toggles persist to localStorage and are read reactively by the Sidebar and the Settings sub-nav. The Launch on System Startup toggle is backed by the OS autostart mechanism (Windows Registry Run key, macOS LaunchAgent, Linux .desktop) and reconciles against the actual OS state after each toggle.

states.name: Page Structure
states.description: The General settings tab renders a SectionHeader with title 'General' and a description, followed by the 'Application' and 'Optional Feature Sets' cards. A third card, 'Workflow Builder', renders only when the advanced disclosure is enabled. There are no sub-tabs or nested navigation within this tab.

states.name: Optional Feature Sets Section
states.description: The 'Optional Feature Sets' card carries the two disclosure toggles that decide how much of the runner is on screen: 'Show advanced automation features' (the verification-agentic loop workflow — Home prompt, Active dashboard, builders, and their settings panels) and 'Show visual GUI automation' (adds the AI Dev / Visual switcher to the sidebar and reveals the image-matching and device panels). Both default OFF and are always rendered.

states.description: The 'Auto-load Last Configuration on Startup' toggle immediately updates its visual state (optimistic), then calls the Tauri command save_auto_load_last_config. On success, a success log message appears. On failure, the toggle reverts to its prior state.

states.name: Launch on System Startup Toggle Behavior
states.description: The 'Launch on System Startup' toggle writes to the OS autostart mechanism (Windows Registry Run key, macOS LaunchAgent, Linux .desktop). Unlike the other toggles, the Rust backend reads back the actual OS state after the write and returns it — the UI reconciles its display against this actual value rather than trusting the optimistic update.

states.name: Settings Persistence Model
states.description: All three settings are stored in the runner's settings.json file at {config_dir}/com.qontinui.runner/settings.json. Settings are loaded asynchronously on mount via three independent Tauri IPC calls. Each setting persists independently — there is no batch Save button. Changes take effect immediately after the toggle click resolves.
